sections.executive_summary: The platform implements the population model of Kim et al. (2026), built from 30 Korean myeloma patients with total and unbound concentrations, at its typical values, with eGFR (CKD-EPI 2021, indexed to 1.73 m2) and body surface area as covariates. Three locked checks compared it with outside group data: CC-5013-PK-001, the same study with matched virtual subjects, and Bridoux 2016 (blind). Mild impairment is consistent; severe impairment is under-predicted in every check's primary scenario; the moderate group was consistent in the first check but under-predicted once the virtual subjects matched the study, and again in Bridoux. Shown for research and education with the moderate and severe bands flagged.
sections.introduction: Kim et al. (2026) modelled lenalidomide in myeloma patients with renal impairment, measuring both total and unbound drug, and proposed model-informed dosing. The platform uses its typical values to compare with Hughes 2019 in the Patient Lab. Its clearance equation can be read in more than one form; the platform reads it in linear multiplicative form, inferred from the paper's reported simulations, and shows the other readings as sensitivity cases, pending the authors' answer. Its kidney measure is indexed eGFR, which the FDA's 2024 renal guidance does not prefer for dosing; the platform runs the model as published.
objectives: Reproduce the published typical-value model for synthetic profiles, including unbound exposure.
Test, under plans locked before computation, whether its kidney-function effect reproduces group exposure outside its source data.
Record which kidney-function bands the model may be shown for without a warning.
discussion: Mild impairment is consistent in every check. Severe impairment is under-predicted in the primary scenario of every check (one sensitivity scenario of the first check was consistent). The moderate group's first result (consistent) did not hold when virtual subjects were matched to CC-5013-PK-001's demographics, and it is under-predicted in Bridoux 2016 as well.

The source study is small (30 patients, 8 with eGFR of 60 or more) and its kidney groups were defined by eGFR, while CC-5013-PK-001 used measured creatinine clearance and Bridoux Cockcroft-Gault; each check built the model's covariates for its virtual subjects as its locked plan states. The Bridoux check carries the same recorded deviation as for Hughes.
The checks compare group means only. The clearance-equation form remains unresolved.
conclusions: The model is consistent with outside data in mild kidney impairment.
It under-predicts exposure in moderate and severe impairment in the matched recheck and in myeloma patients; those bands are flagged.
Further checking needs unseen data and the authors' answer on the equation form.

not_this: Not a regulatory submission and not an independent assessment of the published model. It documents how the platform implemented and checked the model.
